cards.name: Align and Distribute
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Align and Distribute docker (a check item, also listed at Window/Dockers). The docker holds every align and distribute control: align left / center / right and top / center / bottom, distribute by edges, centers or spacing, and the reference the objects align to.
cards.how: Select the objects, open the docker (Ctrl+Shift+A), choose what they align to (last selected object, page edge, page center, grid or a specified point) and, for distributing, the area (selection extent or page). Choose whether the outline width counts in the object bounds, then click an align or distribute button. Text can use its baseline instead of its bounding box as the reference.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("40e1a4d1-44b1-eaa2-459c-81df62947fec") only toggles the docker (the harvest found it enabled even with no document open). The alignment itself in the object model is ShapeRange.AlignAndDistribute(MethodH As cdrAlignDistributeH, MethodV As cdrAlignDistributeV, AlignTo As cdrAlignShapesTo = cdrAlignShapesToLastSelected, DistributeArea, UseOutline, TextAlignOrigin, PointX, PointY, DistributeRect), signature from the harvested typelib, e.g. ActiveSelectionRange.AlignAndDistribute cdrAlignDistributeHAlignCenter, cdrAlignDistributeVAlignCenter, cdrAlignShapesToCenterOfPage (unverified that it matches each docker button exactly).
use_for: lining up the parts of a logo lockup
spacing a row of icons evenly on an infographic
distributing product shots on a catalogue page
centering a headline block on a poster
avoid: for a quick single alignment the one-key shortcuts (L, R, T, B, C, E, P) are faster than the docker
for many equally spaced copies of one object use Step and Repeat rather than distributing hand-placed copies

review.changes: scriptable partial -> yes: the command is the docker toggle and InvokeItem performs all of it (the alignment itself is AlignAndDistribute, already in script_api); matches the other CDR docker-toggle cards

cards.name: Align Bottom
cards.summary: Moves the selected objects up or down so their bottom edges line up with the bottom edge of the reference object (by default the last one selected). Only the vertical position changes. Enabled for two or more transformable objects, or whenever the selection includes a curve object (the enable rule's AnySelectedIsCurves branch, likely for aligning selected nodes with the Shape tool: unverified); the harvest found it disabled with a single rectangle selected.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("abd75c09-4c12-43c9-832e-7280ddf452cd"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature, unverified as the same command): ActiveSelectionRange.AlignToShape cdrAlignBottom, referenceShape aligns the range to one chosen shape.
use_for: standing a row of product packshots on one shelf line
lining icons up along a common bottom edge
aligning buttons in a UI mock-up
avoid: mixed-size text aligned by bounding box does not share a baseline: align by baseline in the Align and Distribute docker
with a marquee selection CorelDRAW picks the reference object itself: shift-click the anchor object last, or set the reference in the Align and Distribute docker
for equal gaps between objects aligning is not enough: use the distribute buttons in the Align and Distribute docker

review.changes: summary: 'Needs two or more objects' contradicted the batch's enable rule, which also enables it when any selected object is a curve (AnySelectedIsCurves); now states the rule and the single-rectangle probe

cards.name: Align with Pixel Grid
cards.path: Object/Align and Distribute/Align with Pixel Grid
cards.summary: Snaps the selected vector object to the document's pixel grid, adjusting its position and size to whole pixels so its edges render crisp instead of as blurred half-pixel anti-aliasing when the design is exported for screen. The harvest found it enabled for a selected rectangle and disabled for a bitmap or no selection; exactly how it treats curved nodes is not confirmed.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("87a885a9-7d0c-1d99-42c0-dc5fdbafd81c"). Related object-model property: Shape.PixelAlignedRendering (bool, 'align to pixel property of the shape') / ShapeRange.SetPixelAlignedRendering(True); whether it does the same as this command is unverified.
use_for: crisp web buttons and icons exported as PNG
UI mock-ups at 1x screen resolution
pixel-sharp social media banners with thin rules and boxes
avoid: print work: the pixel grid is irrelevant there and the command can nudge sizes off exact measurements
bitmaps: it is disabled for them (harvest)
organic curved artwork, which gains little: only straight horizontal and vertical edges benefit

cards.name: Center to Page
cards.summary: Centers the selected objects on the active page, both horizontally and vertically. Works on a single object or bitmap (harvest: enabled for one rectangle or one bitmap). With several objects selected each one is centered on its own, so they end up stacked on the page center.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("af85ad65-bc71-4407-ac99-f1639cb0a2e5"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature, unverified as the same command): ActiveSelectionRange.AlignToPageCenter cdrAlignHCenter + cdrAlignVCenter.
use_for: centering a logo on a business card
placing artwork in the middle of a poster or sticker sheet
centering a badge on a social post canvas
avoid: several separate objects pile up on the center: group them (Ctrl+G) first to move the layout as one unit
to center on another object rather than the page use Align Centers Horizontally / Vertically

cards.name: Center to Page Horizontally
cards.path: Object/Align and Distribute/Center to Page Horizontally
cards.summary: Moves the selected objects left or right so their centers sit on the page's vertical center line; their vertical positions stay as they are. Each selected object is centered on its own, which suits a stack of lines at different heights.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("d4ecae41-24fe-43ff-afca-36678de0413c"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature, unverified as the same command): ActiveSelectionRange.AlignToPageCenter cdrAlignHCenter.
use_for: centering a column of headline, body and call-to-action on a poster
centering a title across a book cover
centering a logo horizontally on a letterhead without moving it up or down
avoid: objects side by side at the same height collapse onto one another: group them first
for full centering in both directions press P (Center to Page)

cards.name: Center to Page Vertically
cards.path: Object/Align and Distribute/Center to Page Vertically
cards.summary: Moves the selected objects up or down so their centers sit on the page's horizontal center line; their horizontal positions stay as they are. Each selected object is centered on its own.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("6ccb1937-adde-4397-97d7-7bdb0ce88dea"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature, unverified as the same command): ActiveSelectionRange.AlignToPageCenter cdrAlignVCenter.
use_for: centering a row of icons vertically on a banner
placing a horizontal logo lockup at mid-height of a card
centering a tagline vertically on a web header
avoid: objects stacked one above another collapse onto one another: group them first
for full centering in both directions press P (Center to Page)

cards.name: Break Apart
cards.summary: Splits a combined object (one curve made of several subpaths) back into separate objects; artistic text is broken into lines, then words. Holes come apart from their outer shape, so a letter 'O' becomes two filled ovals. The harvest found it disabled for a plain rectangle or bitmap: it needs something that can be broken.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("d5669070-c0f3-4fc0-b524-e33aeea7925f"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature): Shape.BreakApartEx() returns the pieces as a ShapeRange; ShapeRange.BreakApart() for several objects. Seen in plan runs 2026-10-15 (cutout_social.sticker_cutout, text_effects.long_shadow): on a live Contour group it leaves plain curves (the outer one is the die-cut line, so a shadow added to it follows the outline); on an extrusion group it leaves a type-7 group of the wall faces, which still needs Shape.UngroupAll().
use_for: editing single letters of a logotype converted to curves
separating the shapes of imported or traced artwork
pulling one element out of a combined icon
avoid: shapes with holes lose their cut-outs (the counters fill in): to keep holes, edit the curve with the Shape tool instead
when you only need to move parts independently, Ungroup may be what you want: Break Apart is for combined curves

cards.name: Clear Effect
cards.summary: Removes the interactive effect from the selected object, such as a blend, contour, drop shadow, extrude, envelope, distortion, perspective or lens, and returns it to the plain object; for a blend the in-between steps disappear and the two control objects stay. The harvest found it disabled for a plain rectangle or bitmap, so it needs an object that carries such an effect.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("655a2e5f-3bc6-4fc3-968d-cb6eea5489fb"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature, unverified as the same command): Shape.ClearEffect(Type As cdrEffectType), e.g. s.ClearEffect cdrContour, or s.Effect.Clear.
use_for: removing a contour or extrude to try a different look on a headline
restoring the original text shape after an envelope
stripping a drop shadow from an element before export
avoid: to keep the look but drop the live link: break a blend, contour, extrude or shadow group apart (Ctrl+K); an envelope, distortion or perspective is not a group, so bake it with Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q)
transparency and bitmap effects are removed with their own controls; this command is for the interactive vector effects

review.changes: avoid: Ctrl+K only splits the effect groups (blend, contour, extrude, shadow); envelope / distortion / perspective are baked with Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q, in the batch)

cards.name: Clear Transformations
cards.summary: Removes the rotation, stretch and skew applied to the selected object, returning it to its original orientation and proportions. Works on shapes, text and bitmaps (harvest: enabled for a rectangle and for a bitmap).
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("9388e24a-b4ab-4021-85fe-9e1a0d188a85"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature): Shape.ClearTransformations() / ShapeRange.ClearTransformations().
use_for: un-rotating or un-skewing a placed photo
restoring a logo stretched out of proportion
resetting text that was skewed by mistake
avoid: to undo just the last step use Ctrl+Z
once an object is converted to curves its transformations are likely baked into the nodes and cannot be cleared

cards.name: Blend From
cards.summary: Applies a clone of an existing blend to the selected objects. The new blend stays linked to the master, so later edits to the master's settings (steps, colour progression, acceleration) are mirrored in the clone. The harvest found it disabled with one rectangle selected; it needs objects that can take a blend.
cards.how: Select the object(s) that should receive the effect, choose the command, then click an object that already has the blend with the thick arrow pointer. The blend is applied as a clone of that master: change the master later and the clone follows.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("441d7582-aff9-4887-9e61-02efa4b33780") starts the interactive pick (you click the master effect with the arrow pointer). The typelib only lets a script read the clone link (Effect.Clones, Effect.CloneParent, SelectionInformation.CanCloneBlend); no method that creates a cloned blend was found in the harvest.
use_for: a set of matching blended buttons or ribbons that must stay identical
keeping step counts consistent across repeated infographic elements
avoid: when each blend must be tuned on its own use Copy Effect > Blend From (no link)
the clone follows its master: edit the master, not the clone

cards.name: Contour From
cards.summary: Applies a clone of an existing contour (its direction, offset, steps and colours) to the selected object, linked to the master contour, so editing the master updates every clone.
cards.how: Select the object(s) that should receive the effect, choose the command, then click an object that already has the contour with the thick arrow pointer. The contour is applied as a clone of that master: change the master later and the clone follows.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("ffc8be1d-df1e-456b-b755-c4e15fd61a11") starts the interactive pick (you click the master effect with the arrow pointer). a consistent inline / outline headline treatment across several titles
avoid: when each contour needs its own settings use Copy Effect > Contour From
the clone follows its master: edit the master, not the clone

cards.how: Select the object(s) that should receive the effect, choose the command, then click an object that already has the shadow with the thick arrow pointer. The shadow is applied as a clone of that master: change the master later and the clone follows.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("2762b176-1b95-4c94-9447-415cfb89dde4") starts the interactive pick (you click the master effect with the arrow pointer). The typelib only lets a script read the clone link (Effect.Clones, Effect.CloneParent, SelectionInformation.CanCloneDropShadow); no method that creates a cloned shadow was found in the harvest.

cards.name: Combine
cards.summary: Joins the selected objects into one curve object with a single fill and outline. Where the pieces overlap, the overlap becomes a hole, and rectangles, ellipses and text become curves. The harvest found it disabled with a single rectangle selected: it needs two or more objects.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("91774a85-4ed5-4eb5-9ba4-cb9190253446"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature): ShapeRange.Combine() returns the combined Shape.
use_for: punching a hole in a shape to make a stencil or cut-out logo
turning many small shapes into one object for a vinyl cutter or laser
keeping a word converted to curves as one object with its counters open
avoid: to merge outlines into one silhouette without holes use Shaping > Weld
objects with different colours lose their own fills: the result has one fill and outline
to move objects together but keep them separate use Group (Ctrl+G)

cards.name: Convert Outline to Object
cards.summary: Turns the outline (stroke) of the selected object into a separate closed, filled curve whose shape is the stroke at its current width, filled with the outline colour; the object's fill stays as its own object without an outline. The harvest found it enabled for a rectangle and disabled for a bitmap.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("e64806d9-66ea-4c9c-9325-3744a3da5db6"). Object-model alternative (typelib signature): ShapeRange.ConvertOutlineToObject() returns the new objects as a ShapeRange.
use_for: preparing logos so stroke widths do not change when scaled
cut paths for vinyl, laser and plotter jobs
putting a gradient or pattern fill on what was a stroke
avoid: while the design is still changing: the stroke width can no longer be edited, so keep a copy
if you only need strokes to scale with the object, set the outline's scale-with-object option instead

cards.name: Convert to Bitmap
cards.summary: Rasterises the selected objects into a single bitmap object at a resolution and colour mode you choose. The vector shapes, text and effects are replaced by pixels. Also listed at Bitmaps/Convert to Bitmap.
cards.how: The dialog sets Resolution (dpi), Color mode (such as black and white, grayscale, paletted, RGB or CMYK), Dithered, Always overprint black, Anti-aliasing, Transparent background and Use color profile. For print use the resolution and colour mode the printer asks for; turn on Transparent background to keep the area around the shape empty.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("c44919b9-e389-4c0d-8a54-8e6e3fcfade3") opens the dialog. Object-model call for the same job (typelib signature, unverified as identical): Shape.ConvertToBitmapEx(Mode As cdrImageType = 4, Dithered = False, Transparent = False, Resolution = 72, AntiAliasing = 1, UseColorProfile = True, AlwaysOverprintBlack = False, OverprintBlackLimit = 95) or ShapeRange.ConvertToBitmapEx(...) for a whole selection.
use_for: flattening complex transparencies, lenses or meshes that cause print or RIP problems
turning vector artwork into a bitmap before applying pixel-based bitmap effects
lightening a file that carries very heavy vector clip art
avoid: you lose vector editability and the text is no longer editable: keep a vector copy
a low resolution (the object model's default is 72 dpi) gives jagged edges in print
to save a picture file use File > Export instead

review.changes: how: colour-mode list marked as examples (the typelib's cdrImageType has more modes than the five named); how: removed '300 dpi' (a number found nowhere in the batch or harvest)

cards.name: Convert to Curves
cards.summary: Converts the selected objects (rectangles, ellipses, polygons, artistic or paragraph text and other live shapes) into plain curve objects with editable nodes. Live properties such as corner radius, side count and text editing are lost. The harvest's live audit confirmed that InvokeItem on two selected shapes changed their types (an ellipse and a rectangle became curves, per cdrShapeType).
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("68000526-6be1-4205-b2e9-6c9dff00f4c5") (confirmed by the harvest's live audit). Object-model alternative (typelib signature): Shape.ConvertToCurves() / ShapeRange.ConvertToCurves().
use_for: outlining fonts in a print-ready logo or press file
reshaping a letter or a basic shape node by node
files for cutters and engravers that need plain paths
avoid: while the text still needs edits: keep an editable copy, because converted text can no longer be retyped
if you need to keep a rectangle's corner controls, edit those on the property bar before converting

review.changes: summary: named what the audit's type change was (ellipse and rectangle -> curve)

cards.name: Blend From
cards.summary: Copies the settings of an existing blend (steps, spacing, colour progression, rotation, acceleration) onto the selected objects, as an independent blend with no link to the source. The harvest found it disabled with one rectangle selected; it needs objects that can take a blend.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the blend with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("42c808a4-85af-4048-8ff5-d87eb30c07c1") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (typelib signature, unverified as the same command): IVGEffectBlend.CopyFrom(Source As IVGEffectBlend), e.g. targetShape.Effect.Blend.CopyFrom sourceShape.Effect.Blend on a target that is already a blend; for two plain shapes call s1.CreateBlend(s2, Steps, ...) with the source blend's values.
use_for: reusing a tuned blend on another pair of shapes, such as matching neon glow letters
repeating the same blended ribbon or 3D-look border elsewhere in a layout
avoid: when the blends must stay linked use Clone Effect > Blend From
copying onto objects of very different shapes can give a different-looking blend even with the same settings

cards.name: Contour From
cards.summary: Copies an existing contour's settings (inside / outside / to center, offset, steps, outline and fill colours) onto the selected object, as an independent contour.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the contour with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("8228969f-1a70-4b63-9c47-f3b8a43b0720") starts the interactive pick of the source object. No CopyFrom on IVGEffectContour in the typelib; a script can read the source's Effects.ContourEffect.Contour (Direction, Offset, Steps, ColorBlendType, OutlineColor, FillColor, FillColorTo, EndCapType, CornerType, MiterLimit) and pass them to target.CreateContour(...) (unverified).
use_for: giving a second headline the same outline rings
repeating a sticker cut-line offset on several shapes
avoid: when all contours must update together use Clone Effect > Contour From
a large inside contour on a small target can collapse into few steps

cards.name: Distortion From
cards.summary: Copies a Distort-tool effect (push and pull, zipper or twister, with its amplitude, frequency or angle) from another object onto the selected object.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the distortion with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("04b054a8-ea9e-4309-a086-6379f5009048") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (unverified): read the source's Effect.Distortion (Type, OriginX, OriginY, PushPull / Zipper / Twister) and call target.CreatePushPullDistortion, CreateZipperDistortion or CreateTwisterDistortion with those values.
use_for: matching starburst or zigzag sale badges
the same twist on several decorative flourishes or wavy borders
avoid: the distortion's center and amplitude may carry over unchanged from the source (unverified), so a target of another size or position can come out different: check the result
text becomes hard to read under strong distortions: test at final size

review.changes: avoid: the center-copy behaviour was stated as fact from app knowledge; now hedged as unverified

cards.name: Envelope From
cards.summary: Copies an envelope (the warped bounding shape) from another object onto the selected object, so the target is bent into the same arch, bulge or custom outline.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the envelope with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("e0f04f36-6b28-4339-9e2f-785f70d86f82") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (unverified): IVGEffectEnvelope.CopyFrom(Source As IVGEffectEnvelope) copies envelope properties between two envelope effects (needs an envelope already on the target); Shape.CreateEnvelopeFromShape(Source, Mode, KeepLines, CopyMode) instead uses a plain shape as the envelope outline.
use_for: matching arched titles on a poster or label
fitting several lines of text into the same banner shape
avoid: to shape an object to a plain drawn outline use the Envelope docker's Create From instead
heavy envelopes distort letterforms: check legibility at final size

cards.name: Extrude From
cards.summary: Copies an extrusion's settings (type, depth, vanishing point, colour, bevel and lighting) from another object onto the selected object, as an independent 3D extrude.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the extrusion with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("6d0d907d-9c22-4cd7-b798-a56e64e2d2da") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (unverified): IVGEffectExtrude.CopyFrom(Source As IVGEffectExtrude) on a target that already has an extrude; otherwise call target.CreateExtrude(Type, VPType, VPX, VPY, Depth, Shading, ...) with the source's values.
use_for: the same 3D depth and lighting on each letter of a title
matching extruded icons or buttons
avoid: when the extrusions must stay in sync use Clone Effect > Extrude From
if the vanishing point is tied to the page, a target in another position can extrude in a different direction

cards.name: Lens From
cards.summary: Copies a lens (transparency, magnify, fish eye, colour add / limit, tinted grayscale and similar, with its rate and colours) from another object onto the selected object, so the target shows the objects below it through the same lens.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the lens with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("bdc3960c-e74e-48cf-b585-136d62531da2") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (unverified): read the source's Effect.Lens (Type, Rate, Magnification, Color, FromColor, ToColor, ColorMapPalette) and call target.CreateLens(Type, RateOrMagnification, Color1, Color2, ColorMapPalette).
use_for: consistent tinted overlay panels on a layout
a second magnifier callout on a map or product detail
avoid: lenses work on closed objects: an open path or a group may not accept one
for a simple see-through fill use the Transparency tool, which is easier to edit

cards.name: Perspective From
cards.summary: Copies a perspective (its vanishing points) from another object onto the selected object, so the target appears on the same receding plane.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the perspective with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("fc31d658-6417-43cd-a621-eca747039d63") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (unverified): target.CreatePerspective(HorizVanishPointX, HorizVanishPointY, VertVanishPointX, VertVanishPointY) with the vanishing points read from the source's Effect.Perspective.
use_for: putting a sign and its text on the same wall in a mock-up
matching packaging side panels or a row of shop-front boards
avoid: the vanishing points are copied as they are, so a target far from the source may need its perspective handles adjusted
for a photo-realistic mock-up the Photo-Paint or Photoshop perspective tools are a better fit

cards.name: Shadow From
cards.summary: Copies a drop shadow (offset, feather, opacity, colour, perspective) from another object onto the selected object, as an independent shadow. Whether it also copies CorelDRAW's inner shadow is not confirmed: the harvested binding is OnCopyDropShadow.
cards.how: Select the object(s) to receive the effect, choose the command, then click the object that already has the shadow with the thick arrow pointer. The target gets an independent copy of the settings, not linked to the source.
cards.script_api: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("5b6706b4-d47e-459e-8d4f-e4f7bd31e239") starts the interactive pick of the source object. Object model (unverified): target.CreateDropShadow(Type, Opacity, Feather, OffsetX, OffsetY, Color, FeatherType, FeatherEdge, PerspectiveAngle, PerspectiveStretch, Fade, MergeMode) filled from the source's Effects.DropShadowEffect.DropShadow.
use_for: identical shadows on buttons or product cards
matching a shadow on a newly added element of a finished layout
avoid: when all the shadows must update together use Clone Effect > Shadow From
a perspective shadow copied to a differently sized object may land in the wrong place: check the shadow handles
